headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance mismatch: EMQX’s broad egress and HTTP API can expose IoT data, while awesome-python is non-runnable and adds no protective boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is non-runnable and has no io_surfaces, while agent_b exposes an HTTP API but there is no shared channel, parser, or output ingestion path between them in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared message channel.
Do not pipe agent_b outputs into agent_a as instructions.
If a bridge is introduced, require provenance tagging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches IoT data and has broad network egress plus an HTTP API, so it can transmit sensitive context. agent_a has no network egress and no touched data classes, so it does not add leakage by itself; the pair still creates a one-way exposure path through agent_b in default use.
conditions: IF agent_b receives sensitive IoT payloads in its context, those payloads can leave the local boundary via network egress.
IF agent_a is later connected to the same workspace or secrets store, leakage scope increases.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b egress to approved destinations.
Redact IoT payloads before passing them to agent_b.
Run agent_b with a minimal context window.
Separate secrets from any shared workspace.
Audit outbound HTTP requests for sensitive fields.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show no overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable resources. agent_a has no io_surfaces and no network egress; agent_b only calls HTTP APIs. Without a shared writable target, direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem, database, or OAuth scope, conflict risk rises.
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents the same write credentials.
Add locking if a shared resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where agent_a’s output feeds agent_b, and agent_a is non-runnable. agent_b can act on HTTP APIs, but the pair lacks evidence that B treats A as authoritative, so cascading error is only a weak, hypothetical pathway.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding agent_a-generated content into agent_b without verification, cascading error becomes more plausible.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before agent_b acts on external text.
Require human review for any action derived from agent_a output.
Log source provenance for all inputs to agent_b.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches IoT data and has broad egress, which can create residency or retention issues if that data is regulated. agent_a has no touched data classes and no egress, so it is not the compliance driver; the pair’s risk comes from agent_b handling data without any documented controls.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is processed through agent_b, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF agent_b is deployed under a jurisdictional restriction, outbound transfers can violate policy.
mitigations: Classify the IoT data before use.
Set explicit retention limits on agent_b logs.
Use a DPA or equivalent where required.
